title: Assert KMS provenance and enforce temporal RBAC grants with audit-sampling override
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes:
- Security: add per-request KMS provenance attestation and validation
- Access control: introduce timebound (temporal) RBAC grants and evaluation hooks
- Observability: audit-sampling override and structured provenance headers
description:
Context: Customers operating under strict data residency and key-governance requirements need stronger guarantees that requests which used tenant CMKs originated from acceptable regions and operator contexts. Additionally, a number of enterprise integrations require RBAC grants that are valid only for tight temporal windows (e.g., emergency operator escalation). This PR introduces a compact server-side flow that attests KMS origin on each request, evaluates temporal RBAC grants, and surfaces an audit-sampling override for high-sensitivity flows.

What this change does: implements a light-weight KMS provenance attestor (pkg/kms/provenance_attestor.go) that validates key metadata and produces a signed provenance header. Adds a temporal RBAC evaluator (svc/authz/temporal_rbac.go) that consumes Linear/JWT claims plus a timebound grant store. Hooks are added to the request pipeline (http/middleware/provenance_middleware.go) to enforce provenance checks for routes labeled with the new annotation `security.kms.provenance: required`. Audit pipeline changes include an audit-sampling override flag (audit/override_probe.go) that forces 100% capture for provenance-failures or temporary-operator sessions.

Design notes: provenance attestation is intentionally non-blocking for routes without the annotation to preserve backward compatibility. For annotated routes, provenance failures return 403 with a structured failure code and include a sanitized audit header to allow downstream forensics. Temporal grants follow an additive policy: an ephemeral grant record is stored in the grant-store with start/end timestamps and a signed grant token is issued; the evaluator validates token integrity + time window. Key origin checks compare KMS key metadata (region, provider, role) against tenant policy and use a small TTL'd cache for performance.

Migration and rollout: feature-gated behind `feature.kms_provenance` and rolled out via console flags. Default rollout: stage -> canary (10%) -> broad. We provide a compatibility shim that emits provenance headers even when checks are disabled to help downstream systems opt-in. Operators must run a one-time migrate script that backfills grant metadata for existing temporary grants (scripts/migrate_backfill_grants.go).

Checklist:
- [x] provenance attestor core implementation
- [x] temporal RBAC evaluator + grant store API
- [x] middleware integration for annotated routes
- [x] unit + integration tests (authz + kms simulator)
- [x] docs: config guide + runbook (docs/security/kms_provenance.md)
- [x] migration script and console flag wiring

Security considerations: signed provenance tokens are HMAC'd with platform KMS-managed secrets, rotated via existing key rotation pipeline. Audit-sampling override can be toggled by SRE and is logged as a privileged action. No tenant secrets are exposed in logs; all provenance headers redact sensitive attributes by default.

Related: ENG-4820 (temporal grants), SEC-117 (audit capture for residency failures).
